meta.concept:
This is a fully 3D open-world title targeting PC platforms with a third-person perspective that integrates hybrid mobility, combining foot-based parkour mechanics like wall-running and vaulting with primary vehicle traversal using rideable hoverbikes. The visual pipeline requires URP to handle stylized rendering, specifically utilizing post-processing bloom and chromatic aberration against the defined neon color palette. A Cinemachine third-person camera system will manage view angles, employing a lock-on targeting mode to maintain focus during high-speed chases and combat engagements without restricting foot movement flexibility.

The architecture relies on eight separate Unity scenes for each act, menu, and boss arena, managed by a district controller that switches ambient audio tracks, sky colors, and lighting based on the day-night cycle manager. Key technical systems include a vehicle controller for hoverbikes, an AI framework handling NavMesh patrol, chase, and alert states, and a bounty system to track multiple live contracts simultaneously. Additional logic layers cover health/shield damage calculation with pickup healing, hologram dialogue events triggered by story beats, minimap radar displaying targets and boundaries, save/checkpoint logic between acts, and procedural geometry tools for generating terrain, road grids, water planes, and room layouts at edit time via ProBuilder.

Development must run on Unity 6000.0 LTS to ensure compatibility with the required physics and rendering features. Recommended tooling includes the Input System for handling complex control schemes across foot and vehicle inputs, NavMesh Agent components for enemy navigation states, Cinemachine for dynamic camera framing, and ProBuilder for constructing tunnel and rooftop districts. Standard scene management and audio spatialization tools are necessary to support the rich layered soundscape and separate scene transitions without requiring additional content beyond the defined eight acts and procedural world pieces.
meta.user_prompt:
Neon Fugitive — a third-person open-world cyberpunk bounty-hunter game for PC.

The player is a rogue AI enforcement agent navigating six districts of a rain-soaked
megacity at night. Each district has its own visual identity: neon markets, industrial
docks, corporate towers, underground tunnels, a rooftop skyway, and the flooded
outer slums. All six districts plus a main menu, a boss arena, and a credits scene
must be separate Unity scenes.

NARRATIVE — eight acts of escalating story beats:
1. Activation: player boots up for the first time in an alley (on_start)
2. First Mark: player receives the first bounty contract (on_enter_zone)
3. Street Chase: player pursues mark through market crowds (on_enemy_death)
4. Betrayal: handler reveals the player is also a target (on_timer)
5. Underground: player escapes into the tunnel district (on_enter_zone)
6. Data Heist: player steals identity files from corporate tower (on_pickup)
7. Showdown: final confrontation with the original programmer (manual)
8. Escape: player reaches the sky-bridge extraction point (on_enter_zone)

AUDIO — rich layered soundscape across eight tracks:
- Pulsing synth main theme (looping music, plays on menu)
- District market ambient (looping ambient, tense urban crowd)
- Industrial dock drone (looping ambient, machinery hum and water)
- Chase adrenaline track (looping music, fast-paced synth percussion)
- Corporate tower tension (looping music, slow arpeggiated suspense)
- Rain and thunder environment (looping ambient, outdoor weather)
- Combat hit and gunshot SFX pack (non-looping sfx, action punctuation)
- Victory sting and credits outro (non-looping music, emotional resolution)

PROCEDURAL GEOMETRY — runtime-built world pieces:
- Procedural terrain for the outer slum district (terrain type, resolution 64)
- Procedural road network grid for market district (road type, resolution 48)
- Procedural water plane for the flooded outer zone (water type, resolution 32)
- Procedural room layout for the corporate tower interior (room type, resolution 24)

SYSTEMS — everything this game needs:
- Third-person player movement with parkour (wall-run, vault, slide)
- Cinemachine third-person camera with lock-on targeting mode
- Enemy AI with NavMesh patrol, chase, and alert states
- Bounty system tracking multiple live contracts simultaneously
- Health and damage system with shields and healing pickups
- Dialogue manager playing all eight story beats as in-world hologram events
- District manager switching ambient audio and sky color per zone transition
- Day-night cycle controller driving scene lighting and NPC schedules
- Vehicle controller for rideable hoverbikes in open sections
- Weapon system managing ranged and melee attack combos
- Inventory and equipment screen
- Minimap radar displaying bounty targets and district boundaries
- Save and checkpoint system between acts
- ProBuilder level generator producing the tunnel and rooftop districts at edit time

VISUAL STYLE: stylized — heavy neon on deep dark backgrounds.
COLOR PALETTE name "NeonFugitive":
  primary   #00F5FF  (player energy — cyan glow)
  secondary #1A0A2E  (environment base — near-black violet)
  accent    #FF2D78  (enemies and hazards — hot pink)
  background #0D0D1A (sky and voids — pitch dark blue)
  trim      #FFD600  (UI, collectibles, highlights — electric yellow)

RENDER PIPELINE: URP (post-processing bloom and chromatic aberration essential).
UNITY VERSION: 6000.0
PLATFORM: PC

audio_cues.gen_prompt: High-pitched electric whine rising in pitch as speed increases, vibrating through the chassis.
Rhythmic clatter of hover-tires skidding over wet asphalt and grinding against metal grates.
Sharp synthetic squeal followed by a heavy thud as feet slap against slick concrete surfaces.
Soft, crackling static hiss layered with faint digital chirps emanating from the air itself.
Deep sub-bass rumble shifting smoothly between industrial drone and distant rain on metal sheets.
Low mechanical whirring of rotors spinning up as enemies transition from idle to chase states.
Subtle digital click-clack sounds as the minimap cursor snaps to new target coordinates.
Heavy hydraulic hiss and grinding gears as the world geometry reshapes during level transitions.

extra_methods.body: _colorStops = new Color[3] { new Color(1f, 0.2f, 0.8f), new Color(0.5f, 0.9f, 1f), new Color(1f, 0.2f, 0.8f) }; _stopTimes = new float[3] { 0f, 2f, 4f }; loopCycle = true; if (_routine != null) StopCoroutine(_routine); _routine = StartCoroutine(RunCycle());

if (!loopCycle) yield break; float t = 0f; while (true) { for (int i = 0; i < _colorStops.Length - 1; i++) { Color startColor = _colorStops[i]; Color endColor = _colorStops[i + 1]; float startTime = _stopTimes[i]; float endTime = _stopTimes[i + 1]; while (t < endTime) { SetColor(Color.Lerp(startColor, endColor, Mathf.Clamp01((t - startTime) / (endTime - startTime)))); t += Time.deltaTime; yield return null; } } t = 0f; yield return null; }
loopCycle = false; if (_routine != null) StopCoroutine(_routine); _routine = null;
